title: The factor-two relation between triangle deletion and packing
decision_reason: Full formulation, independent recent corroboration, source/model comparisons, duplicate review and separated A47 adversarial self-review passed; no unresolved material matching resolution claim located.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: An arbitrary finite simple undirected graph G=(V,E). T(G) is the set of three-edge subsets forming triangles.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every such graph, without restrictions on order, degrees, density, planarity or randomness.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: nu_triangle(G) is the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles, whose vertices may overlap. tau_triangle(G) is the minimum cardinality of an edge subset meeting every triangle, equivalently whose deletion makes G triangle-free.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Prove or disprove tau_triangle(G) <= 2 nu_triangle(G). Both extrema are integral and unweighted; this is an exact finite-graph inequality, with no additive error or asymptotic qualification.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: An unconditional extremal assertion. No algorithm, polynomial running time, or method of obtaining an optimal packing is postulated.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Count one canonical conjecture. Exclude arbitrary hypergraph matching-covering conjectures, weighted relaxations, vertex-disjoint triangle packing, and separate entries for graph subclasses. The edge-decomposition formulation is equivalent and not a separate problem.

source_records.title: Tuza's inequality with three neighborhood types
source_records.version: File's latest commit 97fa6a420f417458e11723c8bceb70f1529e447a, September 14, 2026 08:27:59 UTC, checked via public GitHub API
source_records.locator: Opening theorem; Classification, Finite certificate and Arbitrary multiplicities sections

resolution_comparisons.result: Integral inequality without K3,3 subdivisions; tau<=2 tau* and nu*<=2 nu generally.
resolution_comparisons.difference: The candidate permits K3,3 subdivisions and requires the two integral extrema. The fractional inequalities together yield only factor four by direct chaining.

resolution_comparisons.result: Fractional approximation for blown-up hypergraphs; hypergraphs with nearly t matching-covering ratio despite exclusion of a finite list of forbidden configurations.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Fractional comparison does not prove the integral target. The counterexamples inhabit the broader forbidden-subhypergraph class; the theorem does not exhibit a graph whose actual triangle hypergraph violates Tuza.

resolution_comparisons.result: With probability tending to one for geometric graphs on a cube or torus, the inequality holds when r lies outside an intermediate order-n^(-1/d) interval and below a stated upper cutoff. Theorem 6 limits almost-perfect packing of sufficiently large cliques.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Probability-one-in-the-limit on those radius ranges is not every finite graph. Failure of almost-perfect large-clique packing is not tau_triangle>2 nu_triangle.

resolution_comparisons.result: High-probability validity for every edge-probability sequence p(n), or every edge-count range m, respectively.
resolution_comparisons.difference: The event need not contain every realization or every finite graph. No deterministic universal conclusion follows.

resolution_comparisons.result: For every alpha>0, some beta>0 and arbitrarily large graphs have |E|>=beta binom(n,2), tau>(1-o(1))|E|/2 and nu<(1+alpha)|E|/4.
resolution_comparisons.difference: This contradicts a stronger dense-graph near-decomposition proposal. It forces ratios near two, but does not assert any ratio greater than two. Density beta may depend on alpha.

resolution_comparisons.result: Claims Tuza for maximum degree at most seven, reduced to seven-regular graphs.
resolution_comparisons.difference: No maximum-degree bound is imposed in the candidate. Certificate verification is not required to see the strict scope restriction, and is not claimed here.

resolution_comparisons.result: Specified split partition with clique size eight and at most two active types; alternatively a sufficient maximum-cut inequality, including a seven-edge shadow case.
resolution_comparisons.difference: General finite graphs need not be split or have such a clique partition. The maximum-cut hypothesis is additional, not automatic.

resolution_comparisons.result: Split graphs with minimum degree at least 3n/5; a ratio bound for tripartite graphs with m>n^2/4; factor 3/2 for complete four-partite graphs of order at least five.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Every theorem retains structural or density hypotheses absent from the candidate. Complete K4 is not mistakenly included in the factor-3/2 statement.

resolution_comparisons.result: For graphs whose edges all lie in triangles, factor-two covers are found when nu/t>=1/3, nu/m>=1/4, or m/t>=2. Relaxing specified thresholds by a positive amount would imply the general conjecture.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Those numerical conditions are not automatic. Theorem 1.3 is a conditional implication, not the claimed relaxation.

resolution_comparisons.theorem_locator: Opening theorem and entire written proof outline
resolution_comparisons.result: Extends the fixed-eight-clique split-graph claim from two to three active neighborhood types, allowing arbitrary multiplicities.
resolution_comparisons.difference: The fixed clique and split-partition assumptions remain. This is a more recent restricted claim, not an unrestricted proof. Finite certificates and checker were not independently validated.

mathematical_checks: Triangle sets are edge sets; vertex overlap between packed triangles is allowed.
Cover deletes edges rather than vertices; the graph is finite, simple, undirected, unweighted and unrestricted in degree/order.
The inequality form handles triangle-free graphs without dividing by nu=0.
For K4, any two triangles share an edge, while a matching of two edges meets all four triangles; factor two is sharp.
Fractional LP duality is not integral matching-covering duality. An existence inequality does not itself prove efficient construction.
No asymptotic error, random-graph exception probability, or restriction to sparse/dense graph families is admitted.
Equivalent edge decomposition is one problem. No separate counts for restricted degree, planarity, split graphs or hypergraph restatements.
